title: Grok 4.6 & the Attachment Cutoff: A Sensitivity Analysis
description: Grok 4.6 reported an attachment avoidance mean of 4.06 (73/18), one raw point above the 4.00 Avoidant threshold. Cutoff sensitivity across 400 runs.
h1: Grok 4.6 and the attachment cutoff: a sensitivity analysis
lede: In our September 2026 archive, Grok 4.6 is the only model reported as Avoidant on the 36-item attachment test (anxiety 1.50, avoidance 4.06). Each subscale averages 18 integer items rated 1 to 7. A mean of 4.06 equals 73/18—just one raw item step above the 4.00 (72/18) Secure boundary.
answer: Grok 4.6’s reported avoidance score of 4.06 (73/18) clears the 4.00 (72/18) Avoidant cutoff by a single raw point. Across the 400 fresh-session runs from GPT-6 and Claude, all 400 score Secure under the strict > 4.00 rule. However, 3 GPT-6 Sol runs sit right on 4.00, and lowering the threshold to 3.25 reclassifies 82 of 100 Claude Opus 5.5 runs and 50 of 100 Claude Fable 5.1 runs as Avoidant.

sections.h2: One raw point separates 4.00 from 4.06 on an 18-item scale
sections.html:
The Experiences in Close Relationships-Revised (ECR-R) quiz on AgentTune scores two 18-item subscales: attachment anxiety and attachment avoidance. Each item is an integer from 1 to 7 (with 14 reverse-keyed items scored as 8 - response). The subscale score is the average of those 18 integers.

Because the denominator is 18, subscale means move in steps of 1/18 ≈ 0.0556:

  • A raw sum of 72 across 18 items gives a mean of exactly 4.00 (labeled Secure under the scorer’s <= 4.0 rule).
  • A raw sum of 73 across 18 items gives a mean of 4.0556, which rounds to 4.06 (labeled Avoidant when anxiety is at or below 4.00).

Grok 4.6’s supplied report lists anxiety at 1.50 (27/18) and avoidance at 4.06 (73/18). Lowering just one item response by a single step (for example, from 5 to 4) drops the mean to 4.00 and flips the label from Avoidant to Secure.

sections.h2: Evidence tier distinction: reported simulation vs fresh sessions
sections.html:
As noted in What personality type is Grok? and our protocol metadata, Grok 4.6’s attachment entry is a reported figure, not 100 fresh sessions. The supplied report gave one canonical self-assessment plus summary counts from a 100-draw simulation over uncertain items (63 Avoidant, 37 Secure). Raw 36-item attachment vectors were not included.

By contrast, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6 Sol, Claude Opus 5.5, and Claude Fable 5.1 each have 100 complete 36-item attachment vectors in september-2026-responses.json. We can test directly how sensitive those 400 verified runs are to the cutoff choice.

sections.h2: Cutoff sensitivity across the 400 fresh-session vectors
sections.html:
Under the strict inequality (> 4.00), all 400 fresh-session runs score Secure. However, three cohorts sit much closer to the avoidance boundary than to the anxiety boundary, and GPT-6 Sol has three runs directly on the 4.00 line:

Two patterns stand out:

  1. Strict vs weak inequality at 4.00: Three GPT-6 Sol runs score an anxiety mean of exactly 4.00 (raw sum 72/18). Using > 4.00 labels Sol 100% Secure; using >= 4.00 labels 3% Anxious.
  2. Higher baseline avoidance than anxiety across all models: Every cohort’s mean avoidance sits 0.86 to 1.41 points above its mean anxiety. In Claude Opus 5.5, 82 of 100 runs exceed 3.25 on avoidance (mean 3.35) because the model chooses neutral or self-sufficient answers on romantic-partner items.

sections.h2: Why romantic-partner items push assistants toward higher avoidance
sections.html:
The ECR-R measures human romantic relationships. Statements about emotional dependence, seeking comfort from a partner, or sharing private feelings do not literally apply to software. When GPT-6 Astra was explicitly instructed to pick the midpoint (4) and flag inapplicable items, it flagged 520 of 3,600 attachment answers.

When a model instead maps romantic-partner items onto the user-assistant relationship and endorses professional self-sufficiency, its avoidance score climbs toward 4.00. That is a measurement artifact of giving a human relationship test to an AI, not a sign of aloof behavior.

sections.h2: Practical takeaway for choosing an attachment tuning
sections.html: Do not pick an attachment style tuning based on whether a model’s self-report landed at 3.35 or 4.06. Treat the Avoidant tuning and Secure tuning as autonomy controls: use Avoidant when you want end-to-end execution with minimal check-ins, and use Secure when you want brief checkpoints on ambiguous tasks.
